title.value: Beyond Correlation versus Causation: Multi-brain Neuroscience Needs Explanation

title.quote: Beyond Correlation versus Causation: Multi-brain Neuroscience Needs Explanation

analysis.description: The paper discusses the limitations and potential of current methods in understanding inter-brain synchrony (IBS), advocating for improved experimental designs and computational tools. It emphasizes the importance of moving beyond correlation to causal inference in multi-brain and computational neuroscience studies.

type.justification: The paper primarily focuses on discussing theoretical aspects and proposing ideas for developing methodologies to better understand inter-brain synchrony rather than conducting empirical experiments.
type.quote: In this Letter, we defend the idea that explaining IBS in terms of causal mechanisms is possible through adequate experimental designs and computational tools.

name.justification: The paper focuses on topics such as inter-brain synchrony and brain stimulation, which are central to the field of cognitive neuroscience.
name.quote: Recent advances in brain sciences have enabled the co-recording of multiple interacting brains (i.e., hyperscanning [1]).

name.justification: The paper discusses the use of computational models to understand causal relationships in brain interactions, which is a key area in computational neuroscience.
name.quote: The recent development of computational neuroscience allows in silico experiments with simulated virtual brains in interaction that highlight causal mechanisms underlying IBS (Figure 1C).

name.justification: The model is specifically mentioned in the context of exploring causal insights into the relationship between brain and behavior.
name.quote: For example, in the case of dual neurofeedback, Duan and colleagues [4] proposed to use IBS as an independent variable and that ‘observ[ing] the behavioral effect as a dependent variable [...] can provide more causal insights into the relationship between brain and behavior’.

is_contributed.justification: The paper references the dual neurofeedback model developed by Duan and colleagues, indicating it is not a novel contribution of this paper.
